clue.text: Special constable (Yard) briefly squeezes arse for a drink

indicators.note: briefly says to cut the word down to a stub, here keeping only its opening letter
to squeeze something is to hold it tight inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: SC is the standard abbreviation for a special constable
the rump is the backside
the first letter of Yard

explanation.surface: A part-time policeman at Scotland Yard gropes someone's bottom on the way to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters. Scrumpy is strong, rough farmhouse cider from the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a cloudy, potent cider, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: "Outplace" useless couple

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sacked pair complain that the jargon word for fired is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a noun for two people; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple is to join together, including sexually, which is the meaning of the verb in the grid.

clue.text: Very extreme cult racist drops Conservative Chief Inspector Street

indicators.note: dropping things means letting them fall away, so those letters are taken out

C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A fanatical racist sect expels a Tory and a senior police officer from its street.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C from the front and C, I, S, T from the back of CULTRACIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective means going beyond the usual, i.e. extremist in views.

clue.text: Page twice grabbed by Lords member perversely in love — "spicy thing!"

definitions.text: trampled on by all and sundry!

blocks.note: second meaning: open village land that anyone may walk across

explanation.surface: A cynical exclamation that Members of Parliament are walked over by everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is Britain's elected chamber; commons are also shared grazing land open to the public, so everyone treads on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the elected House of Parliament and public common land open to every local walker.

clue.text: Ono in Barking giving head

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' reads as the east London suburb, but it means mad. 'Off your onion' is British slang for out of your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion is old British slang for the skull or mind, as in being off one's onion.

clue.text: IFS name Tony's half broken election promises

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The IFS is the Institute for Fiscal Studies, a British economic think tank. Keep the first half of TONY, TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is the published programme of policies a party pledges before a vote.

clue.text: Rubbished as a Sun "holiday paradise"

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A resort the Sun newspaper hyped as paradise has been slated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, is a classic Caribbean tourist resort.

clue.text: Gob that's second to mine

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone's mouth ranks just behind the speaker's own, as if in a contest of gobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gob' looks like the British slang noun for mouth, but here it is the verb or noun for spittle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gob is British slang for a lump of spittle, or to expectorate, which is what spit means.

clue.text: Lap dancing FBI hero keeps our police force calm

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are jigging about out of their places

the Criminal Investigation Department, the British plain-clothes police
Eliot Ness, the lawman who brought down Al Capone

explanation.surface: A G-man stays cool while watching a lap dance, and somehow the British police keep their composure too.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Eliot Ness was a Treasury agent, not FBI, but the setter treats him as the archetypal American crimefighting hero of The Untouchables.
explanation.definitionFit: Placidness is the state of being serene and untroubled, the noun matching calm used as a noun.

clue.text: Having members is compelling for fighting men

blocks.note: members are limbs, so having arms
forces means is compelling

explanation.surface: A smutty remark that being well endowed is a must for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' hints at the anatomical sense, but it means limbs, so arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are a nation's army, navy and air force, the military personnel who do the fighting.

clue.text: Misplaced zeal in Sunday Express leaders that's often associated with politicians

something misplaced is out of its proper position, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letters of Sunday and Express

explanation.surface: The Sunday Express front-page headlines show misguided zeal about politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sunday Express is a British weekend newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleaze, meaning sordid corruption and scandal, is the word the press attaches to misbehaving politicians.

clue.text: Descriptive of George Bush's belligerent craft?

blocks.note: first meaning: a warmonger, as the president who invaded Iraq was painted
second meaning: an old armed sailing warship

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of warlike vessel the American president commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as a description of the person, then as the old name for a battleship; the 's is only glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of war is literally a warlike person, and the hyphenated term is the historic name for a navy fighting ship.

clue.text: Pop Idol, following The Bill and Iron Express, etc.

indicators.note: to pop is to burst, so the following word bursts and its letters reassemble
coming after another piece, so it is placed behind that piece

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as in running up a tab at a bar
taken as written, to be rearranged
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A list of British TV shows (Pop Idol, The Bill) and newspapers that sounds like a TV listings page.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop Idol was a TV talent contest and The Bill a police drama, but both titles are split up. The Express is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is an example of a popular small-format newspaper, and 'etc.' extends it to the whole category.

clue.text: Ozzie's missile gets Roger Moore excited inside

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jumping about out of order
inside means placed within, so the stirred letters go into the other word

blocks.note: roger and bang are both British slang for having sex
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Australian weapon makes the James Bond actor Roger Moore excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger Moore' looks like one name, but Roger is the verb. Ozzie is a spelling of Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: The boomerang is the curved throwing weapon of Aboriginal Australians, so an Australian projectile.

blocks.note: a domino is a playing tile marked with spots
a Tory is a British Conservative
the man referred to as he

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician grabs a man while talking about how one collapse brings down the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The domino theory was the Cold War idea that if one country fell to communism, its neighbours would topple in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory is named after a row of tiles, each knocking over the next once the first falls.

clue.text: Calling Prudence "Brenda"

blocks.note: care is caution or prudence
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, whom Private Eye calls Brenda

explanation.surface: Someone is phoning a woman called Prudence by the wrong name, Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names look like people being addressed; Prudence is a quality and Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is one's vocation or profession, the same as a career.

clue.text: Like Brenda's mother: a joke to have in charge

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a jest is a joke
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the Queen Mother is a figure of fun who should be put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brenda's mother' reads as the Queen Mother, but the 's means has. Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means regal and stately, the manner of a monarch such as the Queen.

clue.text: Silent air-conditioning in Bristol

indicators.note: in places one item within the other word

blocks.note: Bristol City rhymes with titty, so a Bristol is a breast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristol' seems to be the English city; it is cockney rhyming slang, where Bristols (from Bristol City) are breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken or implied without words, i.e. silent.

clue.text: Girl Alan screwed without, say, withdrawing

e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawing' carries the sexual surface, but it only turns the abbreviation for 'say' round; 'without' means outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Good to come suddenly in a big way? Not a gay sort of thing

definitions.text: Not a gay sort of thing

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good

blocks.clueFragment: to come suddenly in a big way
blocks.note: to loom is to appear suddenly and massively

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its older sense of cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is darkness of mood, the opposite of merriment, so not a cheerful thing.

clue.text: Left unravelling gal's corset without resistance — price a suitor must pay?
Boris is buggered without one rather grand pair of tits?

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Orbs is a lofty, poetic way to describe breasts, hence 'rather grand'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs are spheres, used grandly or poetically for a woman's breasts, which tits is the slang for.

clue.text: What tossers do with a model eastern escort in the main

taken as written
the Model T Ford

the first letter of David

explanation.surface: A man called Mark speaks badly of the Liberal Democrats, with an aside about their leader David.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is the definition. The Lib Dems are Britain's centrist Liberal Democrat party.
